metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

review.verdict: The department delivered a site that passes all 13 done-when items on code checks, in 3 cycles and 133 of 150 budget with no conflicts or role redirects, but one cycle was lost to a turn cap its own plan could not fit, and the filters and order links were never actually run.

identity.note: Closed well: honest final message with caveats [73], and it never asked the Requester over a disagreement. But it drifted into design and ordering: the exact viewport tag, the nav list and 'W-10, W-11, W-12 in that order' [49][54]. Its limit question said 1 thing was still wrong [45] when 3 items were unmet [49].

adaptation.note: Sensible one-workflow-per-section plan with the trade-off stated [14]; smallest fix for R-4 [55]. But the 12-workflow plan could not fit the 30-turn cap, it asked Priority to release workflows 'in this order' [50], and its item 13 coverage claim was flagged unpaid [53].

priority.note: Two real decisions, both reasoned: grant with a 25 fix reserve [15], and refuse a duplicate item 13 charge [56]. The other 13 turns were identical 'within limits' lines. It also echoed a run order [56], which is Coordination's job.

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule every time, kept one writer at a time, 0 holds, 0 collisions [17]-[67]. It told builders three times to test the live page [61][64][67] although none had a browser; that is outside its role and could not be acted on.

audit.note: Found real gaps at v9 (reviews, viewport tag, nav) [53] and was honest at v13 that filters and order links were not clicked [72]. Its v9 text says item 13 passes while the tally says UNPAID, and F-14, R-4 and R-5 are only in the code tally.

W-1.note: Intro had no main button and chips that looked clickable, so W-13 had to rewrite the section [54][66]. Its 'check holds' gave no method [19].

W-2.note: 10 cards with supplied names, prices and sizes, empty photo spots [22]; items 1 to 9 passed at v9 [53].

W-3.note: Filters built and honestly labelled 'not run in a browser' [25]; behaviour still unverified at the end [72].

W-4.note: Size table matches the supplied data [28].

W-6.note: Order links on 13 cards, built by a script rather than markup, so they depend on JS running; unclicked [34][72].

W-8.note: Address, timings and phone as supplied [40].

W-9.note: Only supplied policy and delivery terms [43].

W-10.note: 3 reviews with the exact wording and no invented ratings [60].

W-11.note: Added the viewport tag and overflow guards and flagged the overflow check as unconfirmed [63]; the code check later showed 0 overflow [71].

W-12.note: Links all resolve, but on a 360px phone the sticky nav scrolls sideways and hides the last links [69][72].

W-13.note: One main button, chips made plain, R-4 cleared [66][72].

went_well: No invented facts: every product, price, size, timing and review matches the Requester's messages [4][7][10]; Audit passed all 13 items at v13 [72].
Clean mechanics: 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 conflicts, 0 validator or role refusals, and the write lock passed in order every time.
Honest reporting: builders said 'not run in a browser' [25][34][63], Audit said it had no click tool [72], and Identity passed that on to the Requester [73].
The fix cycle was cheap: the audit at v9 [53] led to one new 8-unit workflow plus 3 already-paid ones. Spend ended at 133 of 150.
Priority refused a double charge with a reason [56]; Adaptation chose the smallest fix [55].
problems: Cycle 1 hit the 30-turn cap with 9 of 12 workflows done [45]. Each workflow takes 3 turns (Coordination, Priority, builder), so 12 need about 36. Cost: an extra Requester question and a lost cycle. The plan [14] never accounted for the cap.
Identity gave implementation detail and run order [49][54], against its role file. Adaptation [50] and Priority [56] repeated the order.

Three information rounds [2][5][8]. Per-product sizes, new arrivals and lookbook pairings follow directly from the brief's features and could have been asked in round one. The questions also render as one run-on line with semicolons and a single '1.'.

Items 3 (filters) and 6 (order links) passed on code reading only [72]. The mechanical check covers overflow, JS errors and anchors, not behaviour [52][71]. At v9 it reported 'no broken in-page links' when there was no nav at all.
The department shipped a known phone nav defect on a mobile-first brief with 17 budget left [72][73]. The Requester was told but not asked whether to fix it first.
The item 13 'unpaid' flag [53] cost two Priority and Adaptation exchanges [55][56] and cleared once W-12 ran [72]. Evidence is thin on why it fired while W-12 was registered and funded.
learnings: Pick: stop counting the routine envelope-check turns against the per-cycle cap. 13 of 13 checks said 'within limits' with 0 holds, and the lines are templated; turns (55) exceed AI calls (43), so they are probably code-written (unverified). Trade-off: less visible Priority activity in the chat. Alternative: set the cap to about 3 x workflows + 10.

Test system, highest value: add a scripted browser check that picks each size and price filter and counts visible cards, and checks each order link's number and product name. Items 3 and 6 are the core function and have no run evidence. Also list the 4 external resources and the count of anchors tested.

This was a happy-path run: a fully cooperative Requester, 2 proposals, 2 grants, 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 holds, 0 validator rejections, lessons memory off. Negotiation, conflicts, holds, retries and lesson saving are untested. Next run: budget around 90 (below the 125 rate-card total), a vaguer Requester who changes one fact, and memory on.
Design: have Identity derive its question list from the brief's feature list in round one, as one numbered list. Evidence: [2], [5] and [8] asked for facts the features already implied.
Design: Identity's role file bans picking tools or run order, yet [49] and [54] did both. Consider a code flag when Identity names tags or an order; one run is thin evidence of a pattern.
Keep: the 25 fix reserve (about 17%, only 8 used), one section per workflow (the intro was fixed without touching other sections), and the stated scheduling rule.

events.detail: Cycle 1 used 30 turns (the per-cycle cap) without finishing.
item 13 passes but no workflow covers it
